title: Model profile: one model's temperament, as pure data
description: The third axis of a model call (dialect / endpoint / PROFILE). Describes a specific model, independent of which wire format speaks to it and which endpoint serves it. Data, not code: no exam needed, schema validation is its inspection.

model.description: The model identifier this profile describes, e.g. deepseek-v4-flash

contextWindow.description: Total context window in tokens; proportional context budgeting derives from this

maxOutputTokens.description: The largest output the model can produce in one call

acceptsImages.description: Whether this model can be sent images alongside text. A CAPABILITY of the model, so it lives here and not in the endpoint config or the dialect: the same dialect speaks to models that can and cannot, and swapping the model is what changes the answer. Omit when unknown; a consumer then treats it as no, because offering to send an image the model cannot read produces a failed call rather than a degraded one.

nativeWebSearch.description: Offer provider-hosted web search on normal Responses calls. Absent or false disables it. The serving endpoint must also support this capability.

nativeImageGeneration.description: Offer provider-hosted image generation on normal Responses calls. Absent or false disables it; generated pixels are saved beside the ledger.

effort.description: This model's OWN effort rungs, weakest first, in the provider's own words. Lattice keeps one wide ruler (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and places a request on the nearest rung this model declares, so the same word means the same POSITION across providers rather than the same spelling. That distinction is load-bearing: DeepSeek's ladder is high, max — where high is its FLOOR — while on Anthropic and OpenAI high sits well up the scale, so matching by name would send the least thinking to someone asking for a lot. `none` may appear here and is never chosen by nearest-matching: it is how some wires express 'do not think', which is the absence of thinking rather than the bottom of the scale. Omit when unknown; each dialect then falls back to its own defaults rather than a guess.

usageFields.description: Maps this model's NATIVE usage field names onto canonical roles, so ledger observers can aggregate cache statistics across providers without knowing each dialect

quirks.description: Open extension point for model-specific temperament (e.g. parallel tool call support, reasoning-content handling). Consumers ignore keys they do not know.
